subject: What determines the convergence rate of ADVI?

messages.author: ee490f1373633c05
messages.subject: What determines the convergence rate of ADVI?
parts:
For quasi-HMC MCMC stamping (eg NUTS algorithm used in STAN), the rate of convergence is roughly determined by the geometry of the posterior, and in particular:
  • The degree of posterior correlation - high posterior correlations degrade the performance of the sampler if a dense mass matrix is not used,
  • The skewness of the posterior - (eg things which look like bananas will be hard to sample from without a non-Euclidean mass matrix), and
  • The kurtosis of the posterior - heavy tailed posteriors are hard to sample from.


What determines the speed of ADVI convergence using the stochastic gradient descent algorithm?


I presume that the primary factors are the same, and in particular the extent to which different directions have different scales - gradient descent performs poorly if the scales of different parameters vary greatly. 


Does heavy tailedness have an impact given that this is an optimisation algorithm?
